Not tomorrow’s leaders. Today’s examples.

A paragon is one who represents the very best: an ideal, a model, a standard. That is who we are raising, because Scripture never told youth to wait.

The Paragons is the Graduate Fellowship of the Enthronement House Christian Centre, a vibrant arm of the Enthronement Assembly under the directorate of Special Duties. Our mission is whole-person growth through eight pillars, each grounded in the Bible and modeled on Christ, our ultimate Paragon.

8Core pillarsTraining, mentorship, networking and more, each rooted in Scripture.
3Spheres of influenceFaith, career and culture.
1Ultimate ParagonJesus Christ, our model and our standard.

“Let no one despise your youth, but be an example to the believers in word, in conduct, in love, in spirit, in faith, in purity.”

1 Timothy 4:12 (NKJV)

Eight pillars. One standard.

A letter and a circle.

The logo is born from a simple concept with just two elements. Watch them come together.

  1. PThe letterThe first letter in the word Paragon.
  2. ○The ringSignifies all-rounding and all-encompassing, a term identified with a paragon.
  3. =The Paragons signOne simple mark that carries the whole idea.

Color with meaning.

Four colors carry the identity of The Paragons. Open a band to see what each one stands for.

  • Royalty & nobilityLong associated with kingship and divine authority.
  • Spiritual depthSuggests mystery, intimacy and the presence of God.
  • Wisdom & maturityTied to deep thought and spiritual understanding.

“They put a purple robe on Him…” Mark 15:17

  • Creativity & passionA youthful, vibrant color of energy and originality.
  • Spiritual awakeningLinked to transformation and spiritual power.
  • Royal identityA modern extension of purple that reinforces kingdom identity.

Great for youth ministries and creative teams.

  • Purity & holinessRepresents righteousness and sanctification.
  • Clarity & lightAssociated with divine truth and revelation.
  • PeaceA calming, neutral color suggesting unity and wholeness.

“Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow.” Isaiah 1:18

  • Authority & powerUsed in moderation, it reflects strength and seriousness.
  • Mystery & depthCan signify reverence and awe toward God’s majesty.
  • Contrast & balanceHelps highlight purity, light and the vibrant colors.

Black can speak of sin and of the mystery of God, so it is powerful when used wisely.
